title: chain/v1
description: Tamper-evidence seal of a bundle: chain.json, written ONCE at clean finalize (its PRESENCE is the primary completeness marker). Two linear hash chains run over the bundle: 'events' (each events.jsonl line) and 'decisions' (each decisions/NNNN.json file's bytes). Links are appended incrementally to chain.jsonl (one chain_link/v1 line per chained record, fsynced with its record) so a kill -9 at any point leaves a fully verifiable prefix (SCH-3, C3.1). Linear chains, not Merkle: V1 verification is always whole-prefix, and per-record links localize tampering exactly - the first seq where a recomputed hash diverges NAMES the record; the protocol doc's Merkle commitments are Phase-2 multi-party machinery that can wrap this root later without changing any record format. Genesis binds run identity, pack, agent, and config, so a chain cannot be transplanted between runs. Verification always operates on STORED BYTES, never on re-encoded parsed objects. Verifier verdict is three-valued: COMPLETE / TRUNCATED / CORRUPT - never a boolean.

schema.description: Schema name and major version of this document (the seal). Lines of chain.jsonl use $defs/chain_link with schema 'chain_link/v1'.

streams.description: Per-stream chain summary. Genesis (per stream) = SHA-256 of JCS({schema:'chain_genesis/v1', stream, run_id, pack_content_hash, agent_manifest_sha256, run_config_sha256}) where run_config_sha256 = SHA-256 of JCS(bundle_manifest.run_config). Link i = SHA-256 of JCS({schema:'chain_link/v1', stream, seq: i, record_sha256: h_i, prev: link_(i-1)}) with prev = genesis for i = 0.

events.description: Head of the events.jsonl hash chain (see $defs/stream_head).

decisions.description: Head of the decisions/ record hash chain (see $defs/stream_head).

files.description: Whole-file content addresses of every non-chained bundle file (manifests, ledgers, metrics, chain.jsonl itself): bundle-relative path -> SHA-256 over the complete uncompressed bytes. These files are pure derivations of the chained streams + pack, so content-addressing (not per-record chaining) suffices.

additionalProperties.description: SHA-256 of the file's uncompressed bytes.

blobs.description: Counts of content-addressed blob stores. Individual blob hashes are already committed inside chained events (ObservationEmitted.observation_sha256, AgentResponded.raw_sha256), so only counts are needed here. Under the share redaction profile, raw/ blobs may be deleted; the chain remains valid and redaction.json lists the absences.

count.description: Number of stored observation files (= turns).
Number of stored raw response files (attempts across all turns).

complete.description: True iff finalize succeeded and the final event is EpisodeEnd. chain.json only exists on clean finalize, so this is true in practice; a crashed run has NO chain.json and verifies as TRUNCATED from chain.jsonl alone.

root.description: The bundle's single publishable identity: SHA-256 over the JCS bytes of this document with the 'root' member removed. Printed on reports and share cards; a share sub-bundle names its parent by this value.

stream_head.description: Summary of one linear hash chain.

genesis.description: Genesis link value binding the chain to run identity, pack content hash, agent manifest, and run config.

head.description: Final link value after the last record.

count.description: Number of chained records (events: lines; decisions: files).

chain_link.description: One line of chain.jsonl, appended and fsynced together with its record so the surviving prefix of a crashed run is fully verifiable.

schema.description: Schema name and major version of this line.

seq.description: 0-based position: event seq, or decision turn index.

record_sha256.description: SHA-256 of the record's stored bytes (JSONL line excluding its terminating newline; decision file: whole file bytes).

link_sha256.description: This link's value: SHA-256 of JCS({schema:'chain_link/v1', stream, seq, record_sha256, prev}) where prev is the previous link value (genesis for seq 0). Stored so verification can restart from any prefix point.
